_schema.note: Canonical catalog for the mountain biking quiz (mountainbiking.html). Edit this file directly and push — GitHub Pages redeploys automatically. Optional live override: set SHEET_CSV_URL in mountainbiking.html to a published Google Sheet CSV with the same column names. First pass, added 2026-09-20: 8 real bikes sourced live from konaworld.com and an authorized Specialized retailer (cyclingelements.ca). Second pass, 2026-09-22: added Rocky Mountain Element Alloy sourced live from bikes.com, and refreshed Rockhopper directly from specialized.com itself (now reachable via a real rendering browser, unlike a raw fetch) — corrected its price, groupset, and discipline. Third pass, 2026-11-12, via Firecrawl: +17 bikes from specialized.com/ca, norco.com, mec.ca (Polygon + MEC house brand) and bikes.com — now 27 bikes across all five disciplines, including the catalog's first real downhill (Norco Torrent DH A1) and dirt-jump (Specialized P.3, Norco Rampage 2) entries, plus Canadian-brand depth (Norco, Rocky Mountain, MEC alongside Kona). Height ranges on these are estimates (no brand publishes them on the product page); every other flagged field is noted per-entry in _verified. Grow this the same way the other catalogs grew: send specific pages, or ask for another research pass. See DATA.md for full scope notes.

fields.name: string — model name shown to users
fields.origin: string — country of the brand, used for the 'prefer Canadian' filter
fields.wheel: number — 26, 27.5, or 29 (inches); use 27.5 for a mixed/mullet setup (larger rear, smaller front) since none in this catalog are mullet yet
fields.sizes: array of size labels as the brand prints them — XS/S/M/L/XL, but also SM/MD/LG (Kona, Rocky Mountain), S1-S6 (Specialized), SZ1-SZ5 and Short/Medium/Long (Norco), XXS/XXL. MTB brands size by letter, not cm, unlike the road/gravel catalogs. mountainbiking.html maps every label onto the XS-XL scale for scoring (see sizeAlias there); an empty array (one-size bikes such as dirt jumpers) scores on minH/maxH only.
fields.minH: number — cm, lower bound of rider height this bike fits across all its sizes
fields.maxH: number — cm, upper bound of rider height this bike fits across all its sizes
fields.price: number — face-value price in whatever 'currency' says
fields.currency: optional string, 3-letter code — omit to mean USD
fields.availability: 'mainstream' | 'boutique' — mainstream: normal dealer network. boutique: smaller/premium, limited distribution.
fields.frameStyle: 'step-through' | 'step-over' | 'either' — every entry here is 'step-over': real mountain bikes need diamond-frame rigidity for off-road loads, and aren't sold step-through — a categorical fact about the bike type, same reasoning as the racing/bikepacking catalogs.
fields.discipline: 'xc' | 'trail' | 'enduro' | 'downhill' | 'dirt_jump' — the terrain/riding style this bike is actually built for, scored with adjacency (an XC bike scores worse but not zero for someone who said 'trail', etc.) rather than a hard filter.
fields.travelFront: number — front fork travel in mm
fields.travelRear: number — rear shock travel in mm, 0 for a hardtail
fields.groupset: string — drivetrain as sold (e.g. 'Shimano Deore 11-speed', 'SRAM Eagle 70 Transmission')
fields.image: string — relative path or full URL to a product photo; leave empty to show the sketch placeholder
fields.retailerUrl: optional string — a specific product page URL, set ONLY when a human (or this AI, having actually fetched that exact page) has confirmed it shows this bike. When absent, the result card links to a live web search instead.

bikes.name: Fire Mountain
bikes._verified: Full specs (frame, fork, drivetrain, brakes, price) confirmed live at en-ca.konaworld.com on 2026-09-20. Wheel size varies by frame size (26in XS, 27.5in S, 29in M-XL) — catalogued here as 29 since M-XL is the range most adult riders fall into; height range spans all sizes. Weight not published on the product page.

bikes.name: Rockhopper Sport
bikes._verified: REFRESHED 2026-09-22 directly from specialized.com itself (previously specialized.com blocked automated fetches — worked this time via a real rendering browser instead of a raw HTTP fetch, which apparently isn't blocked the same way). Corrected: current real model name is 'Rockhopper Sport' (was catalogued as plain 'Rockhopper'); Specialized's own site files it under Trail Bikes, not Cross-Country, so discipline corrected from 'xc' to 'trail'; price corrected from a stale $800 to the current $1,149.99 CAD; groupset corrected from generic 'Shimano 2x9-speed' to the actual 'microSHIFT Advent 1x9' derailleur/shifters (brakes are a separate Shimano BR-MT200 hydraulic disc set); color corrected to the current 'Satin Metallic Obsidian'. Fork is SR Suntour XCM with size-specific 90mm (XS/S, 27.5in wheel) or 100mm (M-XXL, 29in wheel) travel — catalogued as 100mm/29in since M-XXL is the range most adult riders fall into, same convention as the Kona entries above. Frame is confirmed dropper-post-compatible but does not ship with one, so dropperPost stays false. Image and height range not re-verified this pass, carried over from the prior retailer-sourced entry.

bikes.name: Chisel Comp Evo
bikes._verified: IMPORTANT: Specialized's 'Chisel' line has historically been a hardtail in general product knowledge, but this specific listing (cyclingelements.ca, 2026-09-20) explicitly specs a 130mm Fox 34 fork AND 110mm of rear travel with a flex-stay design, described as 'the lightest, fastest alloy full-suspension bike in the world' — catalogued as full_suspension per the sourced page rather than assumed hardtail. Worth double-checking against a second source if this matters for a specific recommendation. Height range is an estimate for this class of race-XC frame, not shown on the retailer page. Listed as sold out at this retailer at the time of the pass.

bikes.name: Element Alloy
bikes._verified: Full specs confirmed live at bikes.com (Rocky Mountain's own direct-to-consumer site) on 2026-09-22: price, frame (FORM alloy), fork (RockShox Recon Silver RL), shock (RockShox Deluxe Select), groupset (Shimano Deore), sizes, and colors. Height range is carried over as a class-typical estimate — Rocky Mountain's own geometry/size chart wasn't found linked from this product page, so it isn't a page-confirmed figure. dropperPost not confirmed as included stock, so left false.
